name: Controlled Package Complexity
description: Minimize package complexity to make it easier to maintain

name: Reduced Coupling and Improved Cohesion
description: Ensure minimal dependency on other packets and maximize cohesion within the packet

name: Balance of Abstraction and Stability
description: The package must be abstract enough to be extensible and stable enough to be usable

name: Implementation Efficiency
description: The package should be efficiently implemented in terms of algorithm complexity

name: Package Maintainability
description: The package should be easily maintainable

name: Package Size Control
description: Provide a manageable amount of code in the package

name: Change Resistance
description: Reduce the impact of changes in the package on the rest of the system

name: Interaction Efficiency
description: Reduce the complexity of packet interactions

name: Minimized Interface Complexity
description: Provide simple and clear architecture of interfaces

name: Architectural Stability
description: Ensure that the package architecture remains stable and predictable

name: Transparency and Simplicity
description: Make it easier to read and understand the code in the package

name: Code Duplication Minimization
description: Reduce code redundancy and duplication

name: Overload Resistance
description: Ensure that responsibilities are evenly distributed among the classes within the package

name: Ease of Maintenance
description: Reduce package maintenance costs

name: Interface Optimization
description: Minimize the number of interfaces while maintaining functionality

name: Computational Resource Balance
description: Reduce computational complexity within the package

name: Class Cohesion Control
description: Increase cohesion between classes within a package

name: Structural Complexity Optimization
description: Reduce the structural complexity of the package to increase its simplicity

name: Stability and Modularity
description: Preserve the modularity of the package, ensuring its independence and stability

name: Logic Complexity Minimization
description: Simplify the logical structure of the code in the package

name: Testability Support
description: Increase the testability of the package

name: Functional Load Optimization
description: Ensure that the load on packets is distributed evenly

name: Hidden Technical Debt
description: Moderate MI masks high complexity and coupling, indicating accumulating debt

name: End-User Package Complexity
description: Reduce the complexity of the functionality provided to the end user

name: Rigid Core Package
description: A package with many dependents (high Ca) but low abstraction (A) and stability (I) becomes a rigid "core" – changes here risk cascading failures

name: Concrete Overload
description: Excessive concrete classes with high outgoing dependencies (Ce) create rigidity

name: Unstable Utility Package
description: Static utility classes with high instability are prone to ripple effects

name: Interface Deficiency
description: High coupling without interfaces leads to brittle dependencies

name: Large Blob Package
description: Oversized packages with low MI are hard to understand and modify

name: Abstractness Mismatch
description: Over-abstraction in unstable packages leads to unnecessary indirection

name: Error-Prone Logic
description: High vocabulary/errors suggest error-prone, dense logic
